questions.question: What does the Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) framework help marketers understand?
questions.a: Which advertising channels to budget for
questions.b: Which features to prioritise in the product roadmap
questions.c: Why customers hire a product to solve a specific problem in their life
questions.d: How to structure a marketing funnel from awareness to purchase

questions.question: A SaaS company sees churn spike among users who signed up after watching a product demo. Using JTBD, what is the most useful next step?
questions.a: A/B test different onboarding flows to improve activation rate
questions.b: Improve the production quality of the demo video
questions.c: Reduce the subscription price to improve retention
questions.d: Interview churned customers to learn what "job" they expected the product to do — and whether it delivered

questions.question: A health app is losing users to a competitor despite having similar features. JTBD interviews reveal users hired the old app for "motivation through social accountability," not "tracking metrics." What strategic pivot should the marketing team prioritise?
questions.a: Reposition all messaging around community and social accountability rather than data and numbers
questions.b: Launch a price discount campaign to win back churned users
questions.c: Add richer tracking dashboards to differentiate on depth of data
questions.d: Build a referral programme to grow the community quickly

questions.question: What do the letters R, F, and M stand for in RFM segmentation?
questions.a: Recency, Frequency, Monetary
questions.b: Retention, Flow, Measurement
questions.c: Revenue, Funnel, Metrics
questions.d: Reach, Frequency, Marketing

questions.question: An RFM analysis reveals a large segment of customers with high Frequency and Monetary scores but very low Recency. What is the most appropriate campaign for this segment?
questions.a: A referral programme encouraging them to bring in friends
questions.b: A win-back campaign specifically targeting lapsed high-value customers
questions.c: A cross-sell campaign introducing complementary products
questions.d: A new-customer welcome series introducing the brand

questions.question: A subscription box company has limited marketing budget. RFM shows: Segment A (High R, High F, High M) = 500 customers; Segment B (Low R, High F, High M) = 2,000 customers; Segment C (High R, Low F, Low M) = 5,000 customers. Where should budget be prioritised?
questions.a: Split equally across all three segments for balanced portfolio growth
questions.b: Segment C — the largest group represents the highest acquisition volume opportunity
questions.c: Segment A retention AND Segment B win-back, deprioritising broad new acquisition
questions.d: Segment B only — it has the highest revenue recovery potential

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Sales Playbook in go-to-market strategy?
questions.a: To automate outbound sales emails through a CRM
questions.b: To define pricing tiers for different customer segments
questions.c: To give sales teams consistent messaging, objection handling, and process guidance
questions.d: To track pipeline stages and deal progression in the CRM

questions.question: Your sales team closes at 18% from demo stage vs an industry average of 30%. The same playbook is used across all deal sizes. What is the most likely problem to investigate first?
questions.a: The playbook is not segmented by deal size or ICP fit, so tactics are mismatched to context
questions.b: The CRM is not being used correctly, leading to poor follow-up timing
questions.c: Sales reps need more product training to handle technical questions
questions.d: The product needs additional features before it can compete effectively

questions.question: A B2B company is entering a new vertical where buyers have different objections than their existing market. They have a strong playbook for their core segment. What is the highest-leverage first step before launching into the new vertical?
questions.a: Give the existing playbook to the sales team and revisit after 6 months of results
questions.b: Conduct win/loss interviews in the new vertical to uncover unique objections, then update the playbook before scaling outreach
questions.c: Run paid ads and let messaging performance data inform the playbook retrospectively
questions.d: Hire salespeople with experience in the new vertical and let each build their own approach

questions.question: A breakfast brand wants to grow beyond loyal buyers. Which objective best reflects category entry point thinking?
questions.a: Increase discounting so current buyers purchase more often
questions.b: Make the brand easy to recall in more buying situations, such as rushed mornings, kids' breakfasts, and post-workout meals
questions.c: Redesign the logo so the brand feels more modern
questions.d: Focus only on the single highest-converting use case to keep messaging simple

questions.question: A meal-delivery brand is known for “healthy dinners” but wants to increase penetration. Research shows people also struggle with late work nights, cooking for one, and post-gym meals. What should the brand do?
questions.a: Move all budget to performance ads targeting people searching for “meal delivery”
questions.b: Launch a broad awareness campaign with one generic “eat better” message
questions.c: Add more cuisine options before changing communications
questions.d: Build messaging and media around several high-frequency category entry points, linking the brand to each occasion with distinctive cues

questions.question: A challenger brand has strong consideration among category-aware buyers but low unaided recall when consumers describe buying situations. What is the strategic diagnosis?
questions.a: The brand may be differentiated on paper but weakly linked to category entry points, limiting mental availability at the moment of need
questions.b: The brand needs more rational proof points to convince people who already consider it
questions.c: The product lacks enough functional differentiation to justify premium pricing
questions.d: The media plan is too broad and should focus only on retargeting warm audiences

questions.question: What is the primary strategic role of an email/SMS automation platform in lifecycle marketing?
questions.a: To schedule organic social posts across platforms
questions.b: To host long-form blog content and improve SEO rankings
questions.c: To manage paid search bidding and keyword optimisation
questions.d: To trigger personalised messages based on customer behaviour, lifecycle stage, and consent

questions.question: A DTC brand has 50,000 email subscribers with a 12% open rate and 1.5% CTR. They send the same message to everyone. What is the highest-impact lifecycle strategy to improve performance?
questions.a: Segment by purchase behaviour and lifecycle stage, then build targeted flows for each segment
questions.b: Send campaigns more frequently to create more chances for engagement
questions.c: Redesign the email template before changing the messaging strategy
questions.d: Switch to a cheaper platform to reduce cost per send

questions.question: A subscription brand has strong welcome flows but churn spikes at day 45. They have behavioural data such as logins, product usage, and orders. What is the most sophisticated lifecycle intervention?
questions.a: Send an NPS survey at day 30 and manually respond to low scores
questions.b: Send a discount to every active subscriber on day 40 as a proactive save tactic
questions.c: Build a predictive churn-risk segment before day 45 and trigger personalised interventions based on the behaviour pattern behind the risk
questions.d: Rewrite the welcome sequence so subscribers have clearer expectations from the start

questions.question: In marketing, what role does Salesforce primarily play?
questions.a: Customer relationship management — tracking leads, contacts, and sales pipeline
questions.b: Running and optimising Google Ads and search campaigns
questions.c: Publishing and scheduling social media content across platforms
questions.d: Creating and distributing email newsletters to subscriber lists

questions.question: A B2B company generates many MQLs but sales says the leads are low quality. Both teams use Salesforce. What is the most practical first step to align them?
questions.a: Stop lead generation campaigns until marketing can improve quality independently
questions.b: Give sales a higher volume of leads to compensate for the quality issue
questions.c: Define and agree on MQL→SQL qualification criteria in Salesforce and track lead progression together
questions.d: Replace Salesforce with a lighter CRM better suited to lead qualification

questions.question: A company runs 12 marketing campaigns. Salesforce attribution shows email as top channel but sales says most closed deals came from events. What is likely happening and what should they do?
questions.a: The Salesforce data is accurate and events should be deprioritised in future planning
questions.b: Add UTM tracking to all emails so Salesforce can capture click data more accurately
questions.c: Switch immediately from email to events as the primary channel
questions.d: Salesforce is using last-touch attribution — implement multi-touch attribution to see each channel's true contribution across the journey

questions.question: WordPress is primarily known as a?
questions.a: Video editing and production software
questions.b: Email marketing and automation platform
questions.c: Social media scheduling and management tool
questions.d: Content management system for building and publishing websites and blogs

questions.question: A B2B company publishes 10 blog posts per month on WordPress but sees minimal organic traffic growth. Posts are well-written but not ranking. What is most likely missing?
questions.a: More images and visual elements in each post to improve engagement
questions.b: Publishing frequency — they need to increase to at least 20 posts per month
questions.c: SEO optimisation — keyword targeting, internal linking, metadata, and search intent alignment
questions.d: A different CMS that has better SEO capabilities built-in

questions.question: A media company runs a high-traffic WordPress site (1M+ monthly visitors) and faces page speed issues hurting Core Web Vitals and rankings. What is the most strategic solution?
questions.a: Upgrade to a more expensive WordPress hosting plan
questions.b: Audit and reduce plugins, implement server-side caching, deploy a CDN, and evaluate headless WordPress architecture for performance at scale
questions.c: Delete older blog posts to reduce database size and improve speed
questions.d: Migrate everything to a new CMS to start fresh

questions.question: In short-form social video, what is the main job of the opening seconds?
questions.a: Create immediate relevance or curiosity so the viewer understands why to keep watching
questions.b: Display the full product range before the story begins
questions.c: Delay the key message until the end to maximise watch time
questions.d: Use the most polished brand animation to signal production quality

questions.question: A brand cuts a 60-second TV ad into a 15-second social video, but retention drops sharply after the first 2 seconds. What is the strongest creative fix?
questions.a: Add more product shots from the original ad so the value is clearer
questions.b: Boost the same video with paid spend to give the algorithm more data
questions.c: Rebuild the idea for feed-first behaviour: lead with the tension or result, use native pacing, captions, and one clear message
questions.d: Move the logo reveal earlier and keep the rest of the ad unchanged

questions.question: A brand gets occasional viral short videos, but followers do not remember the brand or move closer to purchase. What content system should the team build?
questions.a: Keep chasing viral formats because reach is the main predictor of future conversion
questions.b: Create repeatable content franchises with distinctive brand cues, recurring formats, and product proof tied to specific category use-cases
questions.c: Stop short-form video and shift budget to static product ads with clearer CTAs
questions.d: Post more behind-the-scenes content so the audience feels closer to the team

questions.question: What is the main strategic value of a newsletter publishing platform?
questions.a: Scheduling social media posts across platforms
questions.b: Hosting and distributing podcasts only
questions.c: Building a direct recurring relationship with an audience through owned subscriber distribution
questions.d: Streaming long-form video content to subscribers

questions.question: A B2B thought leader is choosing between a newsletter platform and a company blog. They want to build an audience through content. What is the main advantage of the newsletter model?
questions.a: It creates a direct subscriber relationship, supports repeat distribution, and can grow through recommendations or cross-promotion
questions.b: It offers more visual design flexibility than a branded website
questions.c: It guarantees better email deliverability than any blog subscriber list
questions.d: Newsletter content always ranks better in search than company blogs

questions.question: A marketing agency wants a newsletter to generate inbound leads. They have strong writing but no existing audience. What is the most effective 6-month growth strategy?
questions.a: Gate all content behind paid subscriptions from day one to signal premium quality
questions.b: Publish daily and wait for organic discovery to compound
questions.c: Run paid social ads directly to subscription pages as the primary growth engine
questions.d: Cross-promote on LinkedIn, partner with adjacent newsletters for recommendations, and convert engaged readers with a relevant lead magnet CTA

questions.question: What is GA4 and what is it used for?
questions.a: General Attribution 4 — a cross-channel marketing attribution standard
questions.b: Google Ad Platform 4 — for planning and buying digital advertising
questions.c: Google Analytics 4 — for tracking website and app traffic and user behaviour
questions.d: Google Automation 4 — for automating marketing campaign workflows

questions.question: A site has strong organic traffic but low conversion. GA4 shows mobile users convert at 0.4% vs desktop at 2.1%. What is the highest-priority action?
questions.a: Audit and optimise the mobile checkout and landing page experience for the underperforming device segment
questions.b: Focus all SEO strategy exclusively on desktop search intent keywords
questions.c: Run retargeting ads to re-engage mobile visitors after they leave
questions.d: Reduce paid spend on mobile campaigns to cut wasted budget

questions.question: GA4 shows revenue dropped 22% MoM but transaction volume stayed flat. Average order value also dropped 18%. Paid budgets are unchanged. What should be investigated first?
questions.a: Run a customer survey to understand why people are spending less per order
questions.b: Analyse which product categories are selling, check for discount over-usage, and compare AOV by traffic source to find the root cause
questions.c: Check if the GA4 purchase event is firing correctly on the confirmation page
questions.d: Increase paid budgets to drive more volume and recover revenue

questions.question: A brand changes colours, typography, sonic logo, and packaging style every campaign. What is the most likely strategic cost?
questions.a: The brand weakens recognition because consumers cannot consistently connect assets back to the brand
questions.b: The brand becomes too distinctive and risks boring its audience
questions.c: The brand loses all performance efficiency because algorithms cannot learn the creative
questions.d: The brand should focus only on product claims instead of visual identity

questions.question: A skincare brand has high ad recall but low brand attribution: people remember the ad but not who it was for. What should the team prioritise?
questions.a: Refresh the campaign concept every month to avoid creative fatigue
questions.b: Increase media spend until attribution improves through higher reach
questions.c: Strengthen and repeat distinctive assets: packaging shape, colour system, product cues, and brand codes across executions
questions.d: Add more claims and ingredient explanations to each ad

questions.question: A portfolio company owns three brands in adjacent categories. Teams want all brands to share the same visual system for efficiency. What should leadership evaluate first?
questions.a: Approve one shared system because consistency across the portfolio always improves brand equity
questions.b: Whether shared assets create confusion in memory structures; efficiency is valuable only if each brand still has clear, ownable recognition cues
questions.c: Let each team design independently because distinctiveness matters more than portfolio efficiency
questions.d: Choose the cheapest design system because brand assets are executional, not strategic

questions.question: A team wants to know why buyers choose competitors. Which research design is most useful as a first step?
questions.a: Ask the sales team to rank the top three reasons based on recent calls
questions.b: Launch a large survey immediately with pre-written reasons for respondents to choose from
questions.c: Run qualitative interviews with recent wins, losses, and non-buyers to map decision criteria before designing a quantitative survey
questions.d: Analyse website heatmaps to infer competitor decision drivers

questions.question: A survey asks: “How much do you love our innovative, easy-to-use product?” What is the main research problem?
questions.a: The question is too short to capture enough detail
questions.b: The sample size needs to be at least 1,000 before the result is useful
questions.c: The survey should only be sent to customers who recently purchased
questions.d: The wording is leading and loaded, so responses will overstate positive sentiment and reduce insight quality

questions.question: A concept test shows 72% purchase intent, but the product underperforms after launch. The test sample was existing newsletter subscribers who received a polished product video. What likely went wrong?
questions.a: The creative launch campaign probably failed to communicate the same benefits clearly enough
questions.b: The research overstated demand because the sample and stimulus were biased; the team tested enthusiasm among warm users, not realistic market behaviour
questions.c: The concept should have been tested only after pricing and packaging were final
questions.d: Purchase intent is never useful and should be replaced by social listening

questions.question: In brand and design, what is Figma primarily used for?
questions.a: Running A/B tests on landing page layouts and conversion elements
questions.b: Collaborative UI design, branding, and visual asset creation across teams
questions.c: Managing and publishing the brand's social media accounts
questions.d: Creating and editing video content for social media campaigns

questions.question: A marketing team uses Figma for brand assets but finds inconsistency across designers in how brand guidelines are applied. What Figma feature most effectively solves this?
questions.a: Build a shared Figma component library and brand kit that auto-applies colours, fonts, and styles across all files
questions.b: Share a PDF version of brand guidelines with the entire design team
questions.c: Assign one designer as brand approver to review all work before it goes live
questions.d: Switch to a different design tool that has stricter built-in templates

questions.question: A fast-scaling DTC brand has 3 internal designers and 12 agency partners all working in Figma. The brand looks inconsistent across touchpoints. What is the most scalable governance approach?
questions.a: Create a comprehensive style guide document and re-send it to all agencies quarterly
questions.b: Require all agencies to submit designs for internal review before any asset is published
questions.c: Restrict design access to internal team only and remove all agency Figma permissions
questions.d: Build a central Figma Design System with locked brand components, publish versioned guidelines, and use Figma branching for controlled updates

questions.question: What is a media database or journalist outreach tool primarily used for in PR?
questions.a: Building email newsletters for customers
questions.b: Scheduling and publishing social posts across platforms
questions.c: Analysing paid advertising performance
questions.d: Finding relevant journalists, tracking coverage, and managing press pitching relationships

questions.question: A startup wants press coverage without a PR agency. What is the most effective outreach approach for the first 90 days?
questions.a: Pay for visibility features to increase attention from journalists
questions.b: Mass-pitch every journalist in the database for maximum reach
questions.c: Filter journalists by beat and recent coverage, then personalise each pitch around a genuine news angle relevant to that reporter
questions.d: Only contact top-tier publications first because they validate the brand

questions.question: A scale-up has 3 weeks to secure meaningful press for a product launch. It has a compelling story but no journalist relationships. What is the highest-leverage strategy?
questions.a: Hire a PR agency on a one-month retainer only for this launch
questions.b: Identify 15–20 journalists on the relevant beat, study their recent work, and offer exclusive angles or proprietary data before the embargo lifts
questions.c: Send a press release to the full journalist list and follow up once
questions.d: Avoid direct pitching and rely on founder posts on social media

questions.question: What does a writing quality and style governance tool help marketing teams improve?
questions.a: Email campaign scheduling and automation
questions.b: Writing clarity, grammar, tone consistency, terminology, and brand voice across content
questions.c: Visual brand templates and design assets
questions.d: Competitor keyword analysis and search rankings

questions.question: A content team is scaling from 5 to 25 blog posts per month with 8 writers. They want consistent brand voice. Beyond spell-checking, what should they implement?
questions.a: Create a shared style guide with tone rules, preferred vocabulary, prohibited terms, and examples of approved phrasing
questions.b: Let AI fully replace human editing because consistency can be automated
questions.c: Let each writer use personal writing preferences to preserve individuality
questions.d: Use the tool only for a final proofreading pass before publishing

questions.question: A financial services company uses writing-assistance tools for client-facing content. Compliance requires specific legal phrases that are often flagged as awkward or unclear. What is the correct governance solution?
questions.a: Have legal review all content after writing tools have changed the wording
questions.b: Switch tools until one understands financial and legal language perfectly
questions.c: Turn off writing assistance for all compliance-sensitive content
questions.d: Add required legal phrases as approved terms and train writers on when to override automated suggestions

questions.question: What makes social content “platform-native” rather than simply cross-posted?
questions.a: It uses the same brand message on every platform for consistency
questions.b: It is posted only on the platform where the brand has the most followers
questions.c: It avoids trends so the brand can maintain a premium tone
questions.d: It adapts the idea to the platform’s behaviours, formats, language, culture, and consumption context

questions.question: A brand republishes polished LinkedIn thought-leadership posts on Instagram and TikTok, but gets low saves, shares, and comments. What is the best strategic fix?
questions.a: Post the same content more frequently until the algorithm learns the audience
questions.b: Translate the core idea into native formats: carousels, creator-style videos, comment-led posts, hooks, and examples suited to each platform
questions.c: Stop posting educational content and use only promotional product content
questions.d: Use broader hashtags to reach a larger audience across platforms

questions.question: A social team produces many one-off posts, but performance is inconsistent and learnings do not compound. What operating model best improves social effectiveness?
questions.a: Define content pillars mapped to audience jobs, assign a clear role to each platform, build recurring formats, and review performance by idea, format, and audience response
questions.b: Centralise all posting through one brand channel to make governance easier
questions.c: Let each channel manager post freely so each platform develops its own voice organically
questions.d: Increase posting volume across every platform to create more chances for a breakout post

questions.question: What is an influencer management platform used for in marketing?
questions.a: Finding, managing, briefing, contracting, and measuring creator partnerships at scale
questions.b: Running programmatic display advertising campaigns
questions.c: Search engine optimisation and keyword ranking analysis
questions.d: Building customer loyalty points and rewards programmes

questions.question: A beauty brand wants to run a micro-influencer campaign with creators in the 10K–50K follower range and track performance. What is the most effective operating model?
questions.a: Let creators choose any posting approach and measure only overall brand sentiment lift
questions.b: Manually DM creators and track all results in a shared spreadsheet
questions.c: Use only macro-influencers because individual tracking is cleaner with fewer accounts
questions.d: Select brand-aligned creators, manage briefs and contracts centrally, and track performance with UTM links and creator-specific codes

questions.question: An e-commerce brand ran a campaign with 50 influencers. ROAS was strong, but 80% of attributed revenue came from 5 creators with heavily overlapping audiences. What should the next campaign change?
questions.a: Move the budget from influencers to paid social for more predictable attribution
questions.b: Increase the influencer count to 100 to spread risk more broadly
questions.c: Audit audience overlap, diversify creators by audience cluster, and weight performance by unique reach as well as attributed revenue
questions.d: Double down only on those 5 high-performing creators

questions.question: Why are social platforms increasingly important as discovery channels, not only as feed-based reach channels?
questions.a: They replace website SEO entirely, so brands no longer need search-optimised owned content
questions.b: People use social platforms to search for recommendations, reviews, tutorials, inspiration, and real-life product proof in context
questions.c: Social platforms rank content only by hashtag volume, making discovery easier to control
questions.d: Paid search ads on social platforms are always cheaper than Google search ads

questions.question: A skincare brand wants to be discovered when people search “best sunscreen for sensitive skin” across short-form video and visual platforms. What should the team prioritise?
questions.a: Post generic lifestyle content to increase overall account reach first
questions.b: Reuse the same paid product ad across every social platform for consistency
questions.c: Create search-intent content that directly answers the query, using natural-language hooks, captions, on-screen text, creator proof, and product evidence
questions.d: Focus only on trending sounds because discovery is driven mainly by entertainment signals

questions.question: A brand has strong social engagement but cannot tell whether social discovery contributes to sales. What is the most practical evidence-building approach?
questions.a: Build social-search content clusters with unique landing pages or codes, add self-reported attribution at checkout, and compare branded/search demand around publishing windows
questions.b: Pause all organic social activity for a month and treat any revenue drop as social discovery impact
questions.c: Ask every customer to choose one social platform at checkout as their only source of influence
questions.d: Use the platform’s last-click attribution as the single source of truth

questions.question: Google Ads primarily operates as what type of advertising?
questions.a: Display advertising placed on news websites and publisher networks
questions.b: Pay-per-click advertising targeting users who are actively searching for specific terms
questions.c: Social media feed advertising based on interest and behaviour targeting
questions.d: Influencer marketing facilitated through YouTube creators

questions.question: A B2B SaaS company runs Google Ads at $15K/month but CPL is $320 vs a $150 target. Keywords are broadly matched. What should they investigate first?
questions.a: Increase the monthly budget to generate more total lead volume and lower average CPL
questions.b: Change ad creative to improve click-through rate across all campaigns
questions.c: Move to automated Smart Bidding strategies and let the algorithm self-optimise
questions.d: Review the search terms report, switch to phrase/exact match, add negative keywords, and pause low-performing ad groups

questions.question: Google Ads CTR is strong but landing page conversion rate has dropped 40% over 3 months. Ad Quality Score is unchanged. What is the most likely root cause?
questions.a: The landing page experience has degraded — investigate page speed, mobile UX, CTA clarity, and whether the page still matches the intent of traffic being sent
questions.b: The ad copy needs refreshing to reflect current messaging and offers
questions.c: The keywords have become more competitive and traffic quality has dropped
questions.d: Google's algorithm has penalised the ad account for policy violations

questions.question: Meta Ads allows marketers to advertise on which platforms?
questions.a: TikTok and Snapchat
questions.b: Facebook and Instagram
questions.c: Google Search and YouTube
questions.d: LinkedIn and Twitter/X

questions.question: A DTC brand running Meta Ads has a 1.8× ROAS vs a 3× target. The same 3 creatives have run for 6 weeks. What is the highest-priority fix?
questions.a: Increase the campaign budget significantly to drive more volume and improve ROAS
questions.b: Change campaign objective from conversions to traffic to lower CPCs
questions.c: Add more audience targeting layers to narrow reach to the highest-intent users
questions.d: Refresh creative — introduce new ad formats, test UGC vs polished video, and A/B test hooks to combat ad fatigue

questions.question: iOS 14+ has reduced reported ROAS by ~30%. The team is unsure if Meta is truly less effective or if measurement is broken. What is the correct approach?
questions.a: Reduce Meta budget significantly and reallocate to channels with better measurement
questions.b: Trust Meta's reported ROAS figures and maintain the current strategy unchanged
questions.c: Implement Meta Conversions API (CAPI), set up incrementality tests, and triangulate with third-party attribution to separate measurement loss from actual performance decline
questions.d: Switch entirely to Google Ads where iOS privacy changes have less measurement impact

questions.question: What is the main purpose of conversion tracking in paid media?
questions.a: To guarantee that every sale is attributed to the correct campaign with no uncertainty
questions.b: To automatically create better ads without human creative input
questions.c: To connect user actions to marketing touchpoints so campaigns can be measured, optimised, and compared more accurately
questions.d: To replace business-level metrics like CAC, margin, and payback period

questions.question: A paid campaign has stable traffic and CTR, but reported purchases suddenly become inconsistent across platforms. What should the team check first?
questions.a: Audit the conversion event setup across the website, tag manager, server-side events, checkout flow, and deduplication rules before changing media strategy
questions.b: Pause all campaigns until the ad platform support team confirms there is no reporting issue
questions.c: Increase campaign budgets so the platform has more conversion data to learn from
questions.d: Rewrite all ad creative because tracking issues usually indicate weak message-market fit

questions.question: Privacy changes and browser restrictions reduce the reliability of platform-reported conversions. What is the most resilient measurement approach?
questions.a: Optimise only on the conversions still visible inside each ad platform
questions.b: Combine server-side tracking, first-party data matching, event deduplication, incrementality tests, and blended business metrics to separate signal loss from true performance change
questions.c: Move all spend to the platform with the highest reported ROAS
questions.d: Extend attribution windows until reported conversions return to previous levels

questions.question: Discord is primarily used by brands for?
questions.a: Running and managing paid advertising campaigns for product launches
questions.b: Building and managing online communities with real-time text, voice, and video channels
questions.c: Tracking and resolving customer support tickets and complaints
questions.d: Scheduling and publishing social media content across platforms

questions.question: A gaming brand wants to launch a Discord community. They have 200K social followers but no existing community. What is the most important first step?
questions.a: Start with a curated group of passionate brand advocates, establish community norms, and let structure grow organically as membership builds
questions.b: Run paid ads directly to the Discord server join link to build initial membership quickly
questions.c: Automate all community management with bots to minimise the need for moderation
questions.d: Create channels for every possible topic area from the very beginning

questions.question: A software brand's Discord community has 15,000 members but only 5% daily active participation. The team posts announcements but members rarely engage with each other. What intervention would most effectively increase active participation?
questions.a: Increase the moderator team so there's always someone responding to every message quickly
questions.b: Add gamification with XP points and levels to reward members for posting
questions.c: Shift from broadcast communication to facilitated member-to-member conversations — with challenges, expert AMAs, and peer help channels
questions.d: Move from Discord to a more professional platform like Slack or Circle

questions.question: A loyalty points system in marketing is designed to?
questions.a: Measure employee productivity across the marketing team
questions.b: Reward customers for purchases and actions to incentivise repeat behaviour and deeper engagement
questions.c: Automatically track website analytics and session behaviour
questions.d: Track referral traffic and attribution from partner websites

questions.question: A beauty brand's loyalty points programme has 60% participation but only 15% of members ever redeem their points. Most points expire unused. What does this tell you and what is the fix?
questions.a: Reduce the number of points customers earn to create more perceived scarcity and urgency
questions.b: The programme is successful — 60% participation is an impressive engagement rate
questions.c: The redemption barrier is too high or rewards aren't valuable enough — lower minimum redemption thresholds and introduce more attainable reward tiers
questions.d: Remove expiry dates entirely so members feel less pressure and retain membership longer

questions.question: A subscription business launches a points programme. After 6 months: points members have 12% higher retention but 22% higher support costs and 18% lower AOV vs non-members. What should leadership conclude?
questions.a: Run an incremental analysis to separate programme effect from self-selection bias — high-engagement customers may have joined regardless of the programme
questions.b: The programme is a success because retention improvement is the primary KPI
questions.c: Redesign the programme to only reward purchases above a minimum order value
questions.d: The programme is clearly failing and should be shut down based on cost data

questions.question: What is a referral marketing platform primarily used for?
questions.a: Scheduling social media posts across multiple platforms
questions.b: Managing live chat and customer support tickets
questions.c: Building, managing, and measuring customer referral programmes
questions.d: Creating lifecycle email campaigns for existing subscribers

questions.question: An e-commerce referral programme has a 3% share rate but only 0.8% conversion from referred visitors to customers. Where is the biggest opportunity?
questions.a: Improve the referred visitor landing experience with clearer offer value, social proof, and a stronger new-customer incentive
questions.b: Add more share channels to the referral widget before improving conversion
questions.c: Increase the referral reward to encourage more advocates to share
questions.d: Reduce the minimum spend required to qualify for a referral reward

questions.question: A subscription referral programme has a CAC of $38 including incentives vs $65 for paid ads. But 40% of referred customers churn within 60 days. What is the correct evaluation?
questions.a: Pause the programme immediately because a 40% churn rate is always unacceptable
questions.b: Evaluate LTV-adjusted CAC, because high early churn may make referred customers less profitable despite the lower acquisition cost
questions.c: Increase the referral incentive to drive higher volume and offset churn
questions.d: The programme is clearly successful because CAC is lower than paid ads

questions.question: What is the primary marketing purpose of static billboard advertising?
questions.a: Building broad brand awareness and recall in high-traffic locations over time
questions.b: Targeting specific demographics with personalised, data-driven messages
questions.c: Direct response — driving immediate website clicks and measurable conversions
questions.d: Retargeting people who previously visited the brand's website

questions.question: A DTC brand wants to test billboard advertising in one city before national rollout. How should they measure the incremental impact on online sales?
questions.a: Survey customers at checkout to ask if they saw a billboard recently
questions.b: Compare overall website traffic before and after the billboards go live
questions.c: Run a geo-lift test — compare sales in the billboard city vs a matched control city during the campaign period
questions.d: Track the billboard URL if a custom vanity domain is included in the creative

questions.question: A startup has $50K for OOH advertising and is choosing between 10 premium city-centre billboards or 50 targeted transit ad placements near competitor retail locations. Goal is brand awareness with the target customer. What is the better choice and why?
questions.a: Split equally between both options for a balanced OOH portfolio strategy
questions.b: 10 premium billboards — higher individual impact per placement creates stronger recall
questions.c: Skip OOH entirely and invest the $50K in digital channels with better measurement
questions.d: 50 transit placements near competitor locations — more impressions with relevant audience context at the moment closest to purchase consideration

questions.question: What is a brand activation in marketing?
questions.a: Launching a new digital advertising campaign across social media platforms
questions.b: Sending product samples to influencers for organic content creation
questions.c: Creating an interactive or immersive experience that brings the brand to life for consumers in the real world
questions.d: Setting up and optimising a brand profile on a new social media platform

questions.question: A food and drink brand is sponsoring a music festival with a 5m × 5m space. Which activation approach most effectively creates brand awareness AND shareable content?
questions.a: A QR code linking to the brand website for more product information
questions.b: A simple branded banner display with the brand logo and product prominently shown
questions.c: A traditional sampling stand focused on product giveaways and branded cups
questions.d: An Instagrammable experience combining sampling, interactive brand elements, and a social sharing mechanic with a clear incentive to post

questions.question: A luxury car brand runs activations at major sporting events. Post-event surveys show 78% recall but only 3% consideration lift. People remember but aren't moving closer to purchase. What should strategy address?
questions.a: The activation experience isn't connecting to the purchase mindset — redesign to include test drives, exclusive access, or aspirational storytelling that links the brand to the buyer's self-image
questions.b: Survey attendees about which specific activation element they remember most and double down on it
questions.c: Reduce activation size and invest savings in digital retargeting instead
questions.d: Run more activations to drive recall even higher and let consideration follow naturally

questions.question: In e-commerce and DTC marketing, what is "unboxing design" focused on?
questions.a: Producing unboxing videos for YouTube and social content marketing
questions.b: Optimising the checkout confirmation page experience on the website
questions.c: Designing product photography and flatlay images for the website
questions.d: Creating a memorable physical packaging experience that enhances the first impression when a customer receives their order

questions.question: A premium skincare brand wants unboxing design to increase repeat purchase and referral. Beyond the packaging itself, what complementary element inside the box has the strongest conversion impact?
questions.a: A company newsletter with upcoming product launches and brand news
questions.b: A personalised thank-you card with a loyalty code or referral incentive for the next purchase
questions.c: A branded tissue paper layer for a premium unwrapping feel
questions.d: A detailed product instruction leaflet and usage guide

questions.question: A DTC supplement brand: custom unboxing costs $3.80/order vs $1.20 standard. AOV is $45. Repeat purchase rate is 38% (custom) vs 28% (standard). Gross margin is 40%. Is the premium packaging justified?
questions.a: Yes — the 10-point lift in repeat purchase rate materially increases CLV; model the CLV improvement to quantify ROI and compare to the packaging cost
questions.b: Only justified for orders above $100 where margins can absorb the additional cost
questions.c: The dataset is insufficient — need at least 12 months of cohort data before deciding
questions.d: No — $2.60 extra cost per order is too high for a consumer goods brand at this AOV

questions.question: Which statement is closest to a real consumer insight?
questions.a: “Consumers want convenient healthy meals.”
questions.b: “Healthy meals are a growing market opportunity.”
questions.c: “Our product has 25g protein and no added sugar.”
questions.d: “I want healthy meals, but after work I am too depleted to make decisions, so convenience wins even when I planned otherwise.”

questions.question: A research report contains 40 customer quotes and 12 charts, but the team still disagrees on what to do. What is most likely missing?
questions.a: A synthesis that separates observations from insight, identifies tension, and translates it into strategic implications
questions.b: More raw data so every stakeholder can find their own conclusion
questions.c: A clearer slide design to make the evidence easier to read
questions.d: A final vote from leadership to choose the preferred interpretation

questions.question: A brand discovers that customers say they value sustainability, but purchase data shows they switch brands for small price differences. What is the strongest insight direction?
questions.a: Make sustainability the main message because stated values reveal what consumers truly want
questions.b: Ignore sustainability entirely because behaviour proves consumers do not care
questions.c: Treat sustainability as a supporting trust cue unless the offer also solves a more immediate trade-off such as price, quality, or convenience
questions.d: Educate consumers until their behaviour matches their stated values

questions.question: A brand has a small budget and wants more category buyers to know it exists. Which media goal is most appropriate?
questions.a: Maximise frequency among existing website visitors because they are easiest to convert
questions.b: Maximise effective reach among the target category while maintaining enough frequency for memory encoding
questions.c: Buy the cheapest impressions available to maximise total exposure volume
questions.d: Focus only on channels with immediate click attribution

questions.question: A campaign delivers high frequency to a narrow audience but brand search and new customer growth remain flat. What is the likely issue?
questions.a: The plan is over-serving the same people and under-building reach among new category buyers
questions.b: The creative needs a stronger CTA to convert the exposed audience faster
questions.c: The campaign needs more retargeting to reinforce the message
questions.d: The media budget is too low to measure any effect

questions.question: A CMO must choose between a plan reaching 80% of target buyers once and a plan reaching 35% of buyers six times. The goal is launch awareness for a new brand. What is the better strategic lens?
questions.a: Choose the high-frequency plan because repetition is always the main driver of memory
questions.b: Split the budget evenly because reach and frequency should always be balanced mathematically
questions.c: Choose whichever plan produces lower CPM regardless of audience duplication
questions.d: Prioritise broad reach with sufficient, not excessive, frequency because new-brand awareness depends on exposing many category buyers early

questions.question: A network effect in product growth means?
questions.a: A structured referral programme where existing users invite friends
questions.b: The product becomes more valuable to every user as more people join or use it
questions.c: Social media algorithms amplifying branded content to new audiences
questions.d: A viral advertising campaign that spreads organically through paid media

questions.question: A B2B marketplace has 5,000 buyers but only 200 sellers. Users complain about limited selection. This is a classic chicken-and-egg network effect problem. What is the best strategy to resolve it?
questions.a: Reduce listing fees for buyers to increase demand side activity
questions.b: Focus on one niche vertical where fewer sellers can still create sufficient value
questions.c: Subsidise seller supply first — offer sellers free listings or enhanced features until there's enough supply to attract and retain buyers at scale
questions.d: Run ads to attract more buyers and trust that sellers will follow organic demand

questions.question: A communication platform has strong direct network effects within teams but growth is slowing because entire teams need to adopt it together. What strategy best leverages the network effect to overcome this barrier?
questions.a: Add more third-party integrations to increase stickiness for existing individual users
questions.b: Run top-down enterprise sales by targeting CIOs and IT decision-makers
questions.c: Reduce the price significantly to encourage individual signups without team buy-in
questions.d: Enable cross-team or external collaboration features (guest access, shared channels) so active users naturally pull new teams in through normal workflows

questions.question: What is the purpose of cross-channel lifecycle orchestration?
questions.a: To coordinate personalised messages across channels based on behaviour, lifecycle stage, and customer value
questions.b: To replace product experience improvements with more frequent messaging
questions.c: To send the same campaign through every channel at the same time
questions.d: To maximise short-term campaign volume regardless of customer context

questions.question: A media app finds that users inactive after day 14 have an 82% churn probability. What lifecycle strategy should the team build first?
questions.a: Send a weekly newsletter to every user regardless of engagement level
questions.b: Trigger early-intervention messages around day 10–12 based on last content consumed and usage pattern
questions.c: Email all inactive users a subscription discount on day 14
questions.d: Send daily push notifications to all users starting from day 10

questions.question: A fintech app runs complex journeys across email, push, in-app, and SMS. Some users receive 12+ messages per week. What governance framework should leadership implement?
questions.a: Let each product team manage its own messaging cadence independently
questions.b: Move all lifecycle communication to email only for simplified governance
questions.c: Set a global frequency cap with cross-channel suppression logic, rolling-window limits, and channel priority rules
questions.d: Reduce the total number of message types across all lifecycle journeys

questions.question: What is the primary role of a customer success platform in B2B SaaS?
questions.a: To build email newsletters for new leads
questions.b: To run paid acquisition campaigns for enterprise accounts
questions.c: To track account health, predict churn risk, and manage post-sale customer relationships
questions.d: To analyse SEO keyword rankings and competitor content

questions.question: A customer pattern of 21+ days since login, fewer than 3 active users on a 10-seat account, and an open support ticket is 73% likely to churn. What should happen automatically?
questions.a: Trigger a customer health alert for proactive CSM outreach with a tailored success plan addressing the specific risk signals
questions.b: Send an immediate renewal discount to save the account
questions.c: Send a generic email from the CEO expressing concern
questions.d: Restrict account access temporarily to create urgency for the customer to re-engage

questions.question: A SaaS company has used customer health alerts for 12 months, but annual churn is still 22%. CSMs act on alerts, yet actions are not tied to measurable outcomes. What is the systemic fix?
questions.a: Replace the customer success platform with a different one that has better reporting
questions.b: Reduce CSM caseloads so relationships become more personal
questions.c: Hire more CSMs so every at-risk account receives more attention
questions.d: Define playbooks that map health-score thresholds to specific interventions and track which actions actually reduce churn

questions.question: What is the primary goal of a win-back email series?
questions.a: Upselling existing active customers to a higher-value product tier
questions.b: Collecting product reviews and testimonials from satisfied customers
questions.c: Re-engaging lapsed customers who have not purchased or interacted for a defined period of time
questions.d: Onboarding new customers after their very first purchase

questions.question: An e-commerce win-back series has 12% open rate and 0.8% conversion. Series: Day 30 "We miss you," Day 45 "15% off," Day 60 "Last chance." What change would most likely improve conversion?
questions.a: Add more emails at Day 75 and Day 90 to extend the re-engagement window
questions.b: Personalise messaging based on what each customer previously purchased, and front-load the most compelling offer earlier in the series
questions.c: Increase the discount to 30% in the Day 30 email for a stronger opening incentive
questions.d: Remove the discount element entirely to protect margins on win-back customers

questions.question: A subscription business has 18,000 lapsed users split into: (1) Cancelled due to price, (2) Cancelled for a competitor, (3) Cancelled after a bad experience. What is the correct strategy?
questions.a: Build separate win-back flows: price-sensitive users get a discount, competitive churners get a comparative value message, bad-experience churners get a personal outreach with an acknowledgment and apology
questions.b: Run A/B tests to find which single message works best across all three sub-segments
questions.c: Send a single win-back series with a universal discount to all 18,000 lapsed users
questions.d: Focus budget on acquiring new customers instead of trying to win back lapsed users

questions.question: A brand puts 90% of budget into lower-funnel retargeting because reported ROAS is highest there. What is the strategic risk?
questions.a: The brand may harvest existing demand while underinvesting in creating future demand
questions.b: Retargeting always damages brand equity because it is too sales-led
questions.c: The brand should stop measuring ROAS and use awareness only
questions.d: Lower-funnel channels should always receive the majority of spend

questions.question: A mature e-commerce brand sees paid social CAC rising as spend scales. What budget decision best reflects diminishing returns?
questions.a: Keep spending until average ROAS falls below target
questions.b: Cut paid social entirely because rising CAC means the channel no longer works
questions.c: Increase discounting to restore conversion rate at higher spend levels
questions.d: Compare marginal CAC and incremental lift by channel, then reallocate budget from saturated channels to under-tested or upper-funnel demand creation

questions.question: A board asks why the brand spends on channels that cannot be attributed cleanly to sales. What is the strongest answer?
questions.a: Shift budget only to trackable channels so finance can see direct ROI
questions.b: Explain that brand channels cannot be measured and require trust
questions.c: Use a measurement stack that separates short-term attribution from incremental business impact, including experiments, geo-lift, MMM, and long-term brand indicators
questions.d: Use platform-reported attribution as the single source of truth across channels

questions.question: A subscription page has 9 plan options, similar names, and many add-ons. Users abandon before choosing. What is the most likely behavioural issue?
questions.a: The plans are not discounted enough to motivate action
questions.b: The audience is too broad and should be narrowed before changing the page
questions.c: The product needs more features to justify the number of options
questions.d: Choice overload and unclear defaults are increasing cognitive friction

questions.question: A SaaS pricing page wants to guide most users toward the Pro plan without being deceptive. What choice architecture tactic is most appropriate?
questions.a: Use a clear recommended option, reduce plan comparison complexity, and explain which use case each plan fits
questions.b: Hide the cheaper plan until users click “see all options”
questions.c: Make the Pro plan pre-selected and difficult to change
questions.d: Add more plan tiers so users can self-segment more precisely

questions.question: A checkout redesign increases add-ons selected but also increases refund requests and negative reviews. What should the team conclude?
questions.a: The add-ons are profitable, so the team should tolerate some dissatisfaction
questions.b: Refunds are a customer success issue, not a conversion design issue
questions.c: The design may be pushing choices that users do not fully understand; optimise for informed commitment, not just immediate attachment rate
questions.d: Increase post-purchase education so customers accept the add-ons they chose

questions.question: App Store Optimisation (ASO) keywords are used to?
questions.a: Test different in-app messages for engagement and feature discovery
questions.b: Improve an app's visibility and ranking in App Store and Google Play search results
questions.c: Track which users searched for the app organically before installing
questions.d: Target users in paid app install advertising campaigns

questions.question: A fitness app has optimised primary keywords but organic growth has plateaued. What ASO tactic would help discover new keyword opportunities?
questions.a: Change the app name to include more primary keywords
questions.b: Add more keywords to the primary keyword metadata field to increase coverage
questions.c: Analyse competitor apps for their indexed keywords, review user review language for natural search terms, and test long-tail intent-based phrases
questions.d: Focus on improving the average rating to boost rankings for existing keywords

questions.question: An app's primary keyword ("workout tracker") has Keyword Difficulty 85 and ranks at position 34. A secondary keyword ("home workout without equipment") has Difficulty 52 and ranks at position 8 with lower volume. Where should ASO effort focus near-term?
questions.a: Optimise further for the lower-difficulty keyword where a position 1–3 ranking is achievable, and use the authority gained to gradually compete for harder terms
questions.b: Target both keywords with paid Apple Search Ads instead of organic ASO optimisation
questions.c: Split ASO effort equally between both keywords for a balanced portfolio
questions.d: Invest heavily in "workout tracker" — higher search volume justifies the difficulty

questions.question: What is the purpose of press pitching in PR?
questions.a: Running press advertisements in print newspapers and magazines
questions.b: Paying for sponsored content placements on media websites
questions.c: Distributing press releases through automated PR wire services
questions.d: Reaching out to journalists with a story idea to secure unpaid editorial coverage

questions.question: A startup sends 200 pitch emails and gets 2 responses. The pitch template leads with company background and product features. What is the most likely problem?
questions.a: The email subject lines are too long for mobile previews
questions.b: The pitch is product-centric rather than story-centric — journalists need a compelling "why this matters now" angle, not a product description
questions.c: The company needs more funding and credibility before pitching tier-1 media
questions.d: Journalists don't cover startups without a dedicated PR agency relationship

questions.question: A B2B SaaS company wants tier-1 tech coverage for their product launch. They have an interesting dataset, a strong customer story, and a category-defining POV. What is the most sophisticated media strategy?
questions.a: Send a press release simultaneously to 500 journalists for maximum reach
questions.b: Hire a PR agency and let them manage all media outreach and relationships
questions.c: Offer an exclusive angle or proprietary data story to one tier-1 journalist under embargo, then brief secondary media with complementary angles after publication
questions.d: Publish a detailed company blog post and promote it via LinkedIn for organic reach

questions.question: LinkedIn Articles are primarily used for?
questions.a: Publishing long-form thought leadership content to build professional authority and reach
questions.b: Advertising products and services through sponsored content placements
questions.c: Tracking competitor content performance and engagement benchmarks
questions.d: Managing and scheduling company social media posts and updates

questions.question: A founder writes detailed educational LinkedIn Articles but gets few views. What distribution strategy would increase article reach?
questions.a: Share the article link directly with no accompanying text or context
questions.b: Write shorter articles to improve mobile reading completion rates
questions.c: Post a native text teaser on the LinkedIn feed directing followers to the article, and actively engage with early commenters to boost algorithmic distribution
questions.d: Tag as many people as possible in the article to trigger notification-based reach

questions.question: A professional services firm wants to build "category expert" positioning using LinkedIn thought leadership. They have 3 senior partners who can contribute content. What is the most strategic approach?
questions.a: Have all three partners post randomly whenever they have something to say
questions.b: Focus solely on LinkedIn Newsletters for a more captured, subscription-based audience
questions.c: Post exclusively from the company LinkedIn page to consolidate brand authority
questions.d: Define 3–5 content pillars aligned with buyer pain points, create a consistent posting schedule per partner with differentiated angles, and cross-amplify each other's content

questions.question: Why are analyst relations programmes valuable in B2B marketing?
questions.a: Analyst reports automatically improve Google rankings for B2B brands
questions.b: Analyst firms buy products directly from featured vendors
questions.c: Analyst firms provide free promotional support to all vendors they cover
questions.d: Enterprise buyers often use analyst research to validate vendor shortlists and justify purchase decisions

questions.question: A B2B SaaS company wants to be considered in a major analyst category report. What is the most important prerequisite?
questions.a: Sponsoring analyst conferences to become visible to the research team
questions.b: Meeting minimum market presence criteria and proactively briefing analysts with evidence of customer traction, product capability, and category relevance
questions.c: Having the highest review volume on peer-review sites
questions.d: Running paid search with strong impression share for category keywords

questions.question: A mid-market SaaS company is seen by analysts as a niche vendor. It has strong retention but lacks market presence breadth. What is the most effective multi-year analyst relations strategy?
questions.a: Expand into additional tracked market segments, increase analyst briefing quality, grow the customer reference programme, and submit stronger evidence for vision and execution
questions.b: Commission research that challenges the analyst firm’s current positioning
questions.c: Focus only on peer-review volume because analyst firms mainly weight third-party reviews
questions.d: Increase total marketing spend to improve broad awareness across all buyer segments

questions.question: What does AARRR stand for in growth marketing?
questions.a: Acquisition, Automation, Reach, Retention, ROI
questions.b: Advertising, Analytics, ROI, Reach, Revenue
questions.c: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue
questions.d: Awareness, Attention, Reach, Response, Revenue

questions.question: A startup applying AARRR finds: Acquisition strong (10K signups/month), Activation weak (12% complete onboarding), Retention average. Where should they focus growth effort first?
questions.a: Build a referral programme to leverage the volume of existing users
questions.b: Focus on Revenue by introducing more pricing tiers for higher monetisation
questions.c: Run more paid ads to increase acquisition volume and hope more users find value
questions.d: Fix Activation — improving the lowest-performing funnel stage before pouring more users into a leaky funnel

questions.question: A team applies AARRR to a two-sided marketplace. Buyer Retention is 60% (strong) but Seller Retention drops to 28% after 3 months (weak). Both sides are essential. What is the most important insight?
questions.a: Seller-side churn threatens marketplace liquidity — prioritise understanding and fixing the seller experience, since buyer-side health ultimately depends on sufficient supply
questions.b: Focus on acquiring more buyers to create more demand and pull sellers back
questions.c: The AARRR framework doesn't apply to two-sided marketplace businesses
questions.d: A 28% seller retention rate is acceptable in marketplace categories with high supply

questions.question: What does K-Factor measure in growth marketing?
questions.a: Customer satisfaction after completing the onboarding process
questions.b: The keyword difficulty score used in SEO ranking strategies
questions.c: The cost efficiency ratio of paid advertising campaigns
questions.d: The average number of new users each existing user generates — measuring viral growth potential

questions.question: A product has a K-Factor of 0.6. What does this mean for the business's growth strategy?
questions.a: The product is growing virally and will compound without additional marketing spend
questions.b: Each user generates 0.6 new users on average — the product cannot sustain itself on virality alone and needs additional growth channels
questions.c: 60% of existing users are actively sharing the product with others
questions.d: The product needs a 0.4 improvement to break even on customer acquisition cost

questions.question: A social app has a K-Factor of 1.2 but most viral spread is within existing social clusters, not expanding to new networks. Growth is stagnating despite a positive K-Factor. What is the strategic diagnosis?
questions.a: The K-Factor measurement is incorrect — a K-Factor above 1.0 guarantees growth
questions.b: Increase the referral incentive to push the K-Factor above 1.5 for stronger compounding
questions.c: The referral mechanism has high depth within clusters but low breadth — the product needs features that create bridges between social clusters to unlock compounding network growth
questions.d: A K-Factor of 1.2 always guarantees sustainable growth regardless of cluster dynamics

questions.question: What do I, C, and E stand for in ICE scoring for experiment prioritisation?
questions.a: Impact, Cost, Efficiency
questions.b: Innovation, Capability, Execution
questions.c: Investment, Conversion, Engagement
questions.d: Impact, Confidence, Ease

questions.question: A growth team ICE-scores 12 experiment ideas. Top-ranked idea: Impact=9, Confidence=4, Ease=9. Lower-ranked: Impact=7, Confidence=8, Ease=6. Why might the team choose the second idea first?
questions.a: High confidence in the second idea reduces the risk of wasting resources on a test built on a weak or unvalidated assumption
questions.b: ICE scores should always strictly determine test order without any additional judgement
questions.c: Ease is the most critical factor, and both ideas have similar ease scores anyway
questions.d: Lower ICE scores should always be deprioritised — that's the point of the framework

questions.question: A team uses ICE scoring for 6 months across 20 experiments. High-Impact ideas (8–10) have a 20% success rate. Moderate-Impact ideas (5–7) succeed 65% of the time. What does this reveal about their ICE usage?
questions.a: The ICE framework should be replaced with PIE scoring for better accuracy
questions.b: High Impact scores may reflect ambition rather than evidence — the Confidence component needs better calibration to distinguish validated hypotheses from wishful thinking
questions.c: The team should only run high-impact experiments and iterate faster on each test
questions.d: The team should stop using ICE scoring and adopt a different prioritisation framework

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a strong creative brief?
questions.a: To align the team on the audience, problem, single-minded message, proof, tone, constraints, and desired behaviour before execution starts
questions.b: To give designers a list of visual assets to produce as quickly as possible
questions.c: To document every possible feature and benefit the brand might mention
questions.d: To replace strategy work with a standard template that any team can fill in

questions.question: A campaign includes five benefits, three audiences, two CTAs, and multiple proof points. Creative output looks busy and people remember different things. What is the most important fix?
questions.a: Add more visuals so each benefit has its own memorable execution
questions.b: Launch all messages and let performance data decide which one matters most
questions.c: Reduce media spend until the creative team can simplify the campaign
questions.d: Define a messaging hierarchy: one primary audience tension, one main promise, supporting proof points, and a clear next action

questions.question: A performance team keeps producing ads that convert short-term but weaken brand consistency. Brand teams reject many assets as off-brand. What system solves the conflict best?
questions.a: Let performance teams optimise freely because revenue data should override brand consistency concerns
questions.b: Require brand approval on every individual ad before launch, even if it slows testing
questions.c: Create a shared creative system: non-negotiable brand codes and tone principles, plus testable message, offer, and format modules within those boundaries
questions.d: Separate brand and performance completely so each team can optimise for its own KPI

questions.question: What is the purpose of a creative testing agenda?
questions.a: To produce as many creative variations as possible so the algorithm can find winners
questions.b: To systematically learn which messages, hooks, formats, proof points, and offers move the target audience
questions.c: To compare designers against each other based on campaign performance
questions.d: To test only visual style while keeping the message unchanged

questions.question: A brand tests 12 paid social creatives. One unpolished founder-led video wins, but the team cannot explain why. What should they do next?
questions.a: Code each creative by hypothesis, hook, format, proof type, audience tension, and CTA, then design the next test around the likely reason the winning asset worked
questions.b: Keep scaling only the winning video until performance drops, then start over with a new batch
questions.c: Assume founder-led content always works better and replace all polished brand creative
questions.d: Ignore the result because one winning creative is not enough to change the creative strategy

questions.question: A marketing team produces high creative volume, but learnings disappear between campaigns and each new brief starts from scratch. What operating system should leadership implement?
questions.a: Reduce creative testing and focus on one master brand campaign per year
questions.b: Outsource all creative strategy to an agency so learnings are handled externally
questions.c: Let media buyers decide creative direction based only on short-term ROAS
questions.d: Build a creative learning library that tracks hypotheses, audience insights, winning patterns, fatigue signals, and reusable principles for future briefs

questions.question: What is the strategic role of first-party data in modern marketing?
questions.a: It helps brands build direct, consented customer understanding and activation capability as third-party tracking becomes less reliable
questions.b: It allows brands to avoid asking customers for consent because the data is owned internally
questions.c: It replaces the need for customer research because behaviour data explains all motivations
questions.d: It is useful only for email marketing and has limited value for broader strategy

questions.question: A brand wants richer personalisation, but customers hesitate to share preferences and data. What approach best improves both trust and data quality?
questions.a: Ask for all data upfront during first website visit so the profile is complete immediately
questions.b: Create a clear value exchange, granular preference choices, and transparent explanations of how the data improves the customer experience
questions.c: Hide data requests inside long account forms to avoid drawing attention to them
questions.d: Personalise based only on inferred behaviour and avoid asking customers directly

questions.question: A brand wants to run personalisation and retargeting using behavioural data, but 55% of EU visitors reject non-essential cookies. What is the most strategic compliant response?
questions.a: Reduce consent layers in the banner to make opt-in more likely
questions.b: Personalise only for the consenting 45% and ignore everyone else
questions.c: Build first-party data through authenticated experiences, quizzes, and preference centres, then use modelled audiences for non-consenting segments
questions.d: Abandon on-site personalisation and move all personalisation to email

questions.question: What is the safest general role for generative AI in a marketing workflow?
questions.a: Act as an accelerator for ideation, drafting, editing, variation, summarisation, and structuring, while humans own strategy, facts, judgement, and final approval
questions.b: Fully automate paid media optimisation, budget allocation, and campaign governance without human review
questions.c: Schedule and publish all social posts automatically across platforms without a content calendar
questions.d: Track website sessions and conversion events as a replacement for analytics tools

questions.question: A content team publishes AI-generated blog posts without human review. After 3 months, organic rankings drop and bounce rates increase. What is the most likely cause?
questions.a: ChatGPT doesn't apply SEO best practices by default in its output
questions.b: AI-generated content without human editing often lacks specificity, expert insight, and original perspective — leading to thin, generic content that underperforms
questions.c: The blog posts are too long and need to be significantly shorter for search intent
questions.d: Google's algorithm flags and demotes all AI-generated content regardless of quality

questions.question: A B2B brand wants generative-AI-assisted content to establish genuine thought leadership in a niche technical market. They have SMEs but limited content team capacity. What is the most defensible production model?
questions.a: Use ChatGPT only for editing and proofreading, never for original content creation
questions.b: Have ChatGPT write all content independently to scale output across topic areas
questions.c: Avoid AI content tools entirely to maintain authenticity and expert positioning
questions.d: Use generative AI as an editorial accelerator — SMEs provide raw insights and frameworks, AI structures and drafts, human editors fact-check and inject unique expert perspective

questions.question: A premium product page lists many technical features but conversion is low. Reviews show buyers are unsure whether the product is “worth it.” What is missing?
questions.a: A stronger perceived-value bridge: outcomes, proof, comparison anchors, and risk reduction that translate features into felt value
questions.b: More technical specifications so buyers can evaluate quality objectively
questions.c: A larger discount to make the value obvious
questions.d: A shorter page because premium buyers do not read detailed information

questions.question: A new wellness brand has strong claims but low conversion because buyers distrust the category. What should the messaging prioritise?
questions.a: More emotional storytelling so consumers feel inspired before evaluating proof
questions.b: Credibility architecture: evidence, transparent limitations, expert validation, reviews, and clear risk reversal
questions.c: A stronger urgency offer to overcome hesitation
questions.d: Broader awareness media because trust only grows through repeated exposure

questions.question: A brand can increase short-term conversion by using aggressive scarcity messages, but qualitative research shows customers already suspect the category of manipulation. What is the best decision?
questions.a: Use scarcity while it works, then refresh the message once performance declines
questions.b: Remove all urgency mechanics because they are always unethical
questions.c: Shift to performance channels where trust concerns are less visible
questions.d: Avoid tactics that undermine trust; use transparent urgency only when real, and build value through proof and confidence signals

questions.question: A team is launching a new product with limited budget. What should be sequenced before scaling paid acquisition?
questions.a: Maximise reach immediately to learn from a large audience
questions.b: Validate the target segment, core message, offer, and conversion path with a smaller launch cohort
questions.c: Build every planned feature before any market exposure
questions.d: Wait until competitors react so the team can position against them

questions.question: A product launch gets strong PR but weak trial signups. The landing page message differs from the press narrative. What is the highest-leverage fix?
questions.a: Buy more traffic while awareness is high
questions.b: Send a second press release explaining the product features in more detail
questions.c: Align the launch story, landing page, proof, and CTA around one clear promise so attention converts into action
questions.d: Delay conversion goals because PR is mainly for awareness

questions.question: A company plans to enter three segments at launch because the product could serve all of them. Resources are limited and messaging differs by segment. What is the strategic risk?
questions.a: The launch may spread learning, budget, and positioning too thin; choose a beachhead segment first and expand after proof
questions.b: The company should launch broadly because a larger TAM improves investor confidence
questions.c: The product team should build separate feature sets for all three segments before launch
questions.d: Sales should decide segment priority after the first quarter of inbound demand

questions.question: Cart recovery in e-commerce marketing refers to?
questions.a: Recovering disputed charges and refunded orders through customer service
questions.b: Analysing which specific products are most frequently removed from carts before checkout
questions.c: Physically recovering lost or misplaced packages from shipping carriers
questions.d: Automated campaigns targeting shoppers who added items to cart but didn't complete the purchase

questions.question: A brand's cart recovery email sends one email 24 hours after abandonment with no incentive. Open rate 18%, recovery 2.8%. What change would most likely improve recovery rate?
questions.a: Send the first recovery email within 1 hour of abandonment with a personalised product reminder
questions.b: Increase the discount in the recovery email from 0% to 30% to incentivise return
questions.c: Extend the series to three emails: day 1, day 3, and day 7 after abandonment
questions.d: Move from email to SMS for cart recovery as it has higher open rates

questions.question: A fashion brand has high cart abandonment for items over $200. Post-abandonment surveys show price is the primary objection. They want to recover carts without training customers to abandon for discounts. What is the most sophisticated strategy?
questions.a: Improve product photography to increase the perceived value and justify the price
questions.b: Remove all high-priced items from the cart recovery flow entirely
