questions.c: Segment by AOV — offer flexible payment options (BNPL, instalments) or a small time-limited incentive only for first-time abandoners, and withhold discounts from repeat abandoners
questions.d: Offer 20% off in the first cart recovery email to all abandoners of high-value items

questions.question: Dynamic pricing in e-commerce means?
questions.a: Adjusting prices in real time based on demand, competition, inventory, or customer behaviour
questions.b: Offering different prices in different countries or currency regions
questions.c: Setting premium prices for premium-tier products across the catalogue
questions.d: Randomly changing prices to test customer price sensitivity reactions

questions.question: A hotel brand wants to implement dynamic pricing. During peak season, rooms are 95% booked weeks in advance. During off-peak, occupancy is 40%. What pricing strategy would increase total annual revenue?
questions.a: Set a single competitive price year-round for simplicity and consistency
questions.b: Lower prices during peak season to attract more customers and improve review volume
questions.c: Only adjust prices reactively based on competitors' pricing changes
questions.d: Implement demand-based pricing — raise prices as occupancy increases during peak, offer early-booking and flexible-rate incentives during off-peak to stimulate demand

questions.question: An e-commerce brand implements dynamic pricing with a 12% revenue uplift in Q1. But customer satisfaction drops and "unfair pricing" complaints increase 34%. How should leadership respond?
questions.a: Revert to static pricing entirely to protect the customer relationship
questions.b: Implement price transparency mechanics — communicate pricing reasons clearly, set floors/ceilings to limit extreme swings, and exclude loyal customers from the most aggressive dynamic ranges
questions.c: Accept the complaints as an acceptable cost of the revenue improvement
questions.d: Only apply dynamic pricing to new customers and exempt existing customers from fluctuations

questions.question: What is a subscription management platform primarily used for in e-commerce?
questions.a: Running customer loyalty points and rewards programmes only
questions.b: Managing pay-per-click campaigns and media budgets
questions.c: Optimising one-time checkout pages for non-subscription purchases
questions.d: Powering recurring billing, subscription changes, cancellation flows, and retention insights

questions.question: A DTC brand launches a subscription product and sees 28% month-1 churn after three months. What is the highest-leverage first area to investigate?
questions.a: Reduce the subscription price immediately to improve retention
questions.b: Add more subscription interval options before diagnosing the churn pattern
questions.c: Analyse the subscriber journey and cancellation reasons to identify expectation gaps, usage friction, or value mismatch
questions.d: Run re-subscription ads to win back recently churned subscribers

questions.question: A DTC company has three subscriber segments: Monthly (40% of subscribers, 35% churn), every 2 months (35%, 18% churn), and quarterly (25%, 8% churn). They want to migrate monthly subscribers to longer intervals. What is the most nuanced approach?
questions.a: Force all monthly subscribers to migrate to quarterly intervals immediately
questions.b: Model LTV impact by segment, offer monthly subscribers a personalised incentive to shift to bi-monthly, and frame the migration as convenience rather than a discount
questions.c: Remove the monthly subscription option entirely to eliminate high churn
questions.d: Keep all intervals as-is and focus only on reducing monthly churn through retention emails

questions.question: What does an ABM intent platform help B2B marketing and sales teams do?
questions.a: Optimise social media ads for consumer purchases
questions.b: Build SDR email sequences without account prioritisation
questions.c: Identify which target accounts appear to be in-market based on account-level intent and engagement signals
questions.d: Improve email deliverability and inbox placement

questions.question: A B2B SaaS company has 500 accounts showing buying intent, but the SDR team can run only 50 outreach sequences per week. How should they prioritise?
questions.a: Prioritise accounts with the strongest intent, ICP fit, and recent spikes in topics directly related to the product’s problem space
questions.b: Start with the 50 largest companies by annual revenue
questions.c: Reach out to the 50 most recently flagged accounts regardless of fit
questions.d: Pick the 50 accounts geographically closest to the sales team

questions.question: After 6 months, intent-prioritised accounts show 31% shorter sales cycles but 18% lower average deal size. Revenue is slightly higher overall. What strategic question should the CMO raise before expanding investment?
questions.a: Lower deal sizes prove account quality is worse, so the programme should be reduced
questions.b: The data clearly proves the programme works, so investment should expand immediately
questions.c: Shorter sales cycle should become the only KPI for the programme
questions.d: Is the programme capturing existing demand rather than creating new demand, and is it missing larger untapped accounts with longer buying cycles?

questions.question: What does third-party intent data provide to B2B marketers?
questions.a: Signals that companies are researching specific topics across external web sources
questions.b: Website analytics for owned properties only
questions.c: Social media engagement metrics for brand pages
questions.d: Email open and click data for marketing campaigns

questions.question: A B2B security company targets accounts researching “cybersecurity compliance.” Reach is high but conversion is low. What is the most likely issue?
questions.a: The landing page should be changed before evaluating account fit
questions.b: The signal shows generic research behaviour, so the team must layer in ICP filters such as size, industry, tech stack, and buying context
questions.c: Intent data is inherently inaccurate and should not be used
questions.d: The ad creative is the only likely problem

questions.question: A company runs ABM campaigns using third-party intent data. Pipeline influenced by intent accounts is growing, but win rates have not improved. Sales says accounts are not ready when SDRs reach out. What does this suggest?
questions.a: The company should replace intent data with another provider
questions.b: The intent data provider is not relevant to the category
questions.c: SDRs only need more product knowledge training
questions.d: Intent signal does not equal purchase readiness; the programme needs a nurture layer and clearer interpretation of signal quality before SDR outreach

questions.question: What is a sales enablement platform designed to help marketing and sales teams do?
questions.a: Build and A/B test demand-generation landing pages
questions.b: Organise, deliver, and measure sales content so reps use the right material for the right conversation
questions.c: Manage customer support tickets and SLA performance
questions.d: Automate paid advertising campaigns across all channels

questions.question: A B2B company creates 50+ sales assets per quarter. Reps keep using outdated materials and building off-brand decks. How should a sales enablement system solve this?
questions.a: Give sales reps a design tool so they can create their own branded materials independently
questions.b: Limit marketing to fewer assets per quarter without changing access or governance
questions.c: Create a central controlled content hub with versioning, search, usage tracking, and visibility into which assets support won deals
questions.d: Automatically update every sales deck on a quarterly publishing schedule

questions.question: Enablement analytics show 60% of sales content is never used, while 8 assets appear in 74% of won deals. Marketing produces content based mostly on product launches. What structural change is needed?
questions.a: Let sales vote each quarter on what content marketing should make
questions.b: Keep only those 8 assets and retire everything else immediately
questions.c: Give sales unlimited permission to create and publish their own enablement content
questions.d: Shift to a data-driven content strategy based on buyer needs by deal stage, retire low-usage assets, and produce more of the asset types correlated with wins

questions.question: What does TOFU stand for in funnel marketing?
questions.a: Top-of-Funnel
questions.b: Traffic Optimisation for Users
questions.c: Targeted Outbound Follow-Up
questions.d: Total Output for Users

questions.question: A prospect has read three blog posts, watched a webinar, and downloaded a comparison guide. Which funnel stage best describes them, and what content should they receive next?
questions.a: Re-engagement — they have been in the funnel too long and need a discount
questions.b: MOFU — they are evaluating options and should receive a case study or demo offer
questions.c: TOFU — they need more awareness content like explainer videos
questions.d: BOFU — they are ready to buy and should receive a pricing page link

questions.question: A content team produces mostly TOFU blog posts that drive high traffic but low pipeline. Leadership wants more revenue impact. What is the most strategic structural fix?
questions.a: Gate all blog content behind a lead form to capture more contacts
questions.b: Add CTAs to every blog post redirecting to the pricing page
questions.c: Audit which TOFU topics attract the ICP, then build MOFU and BOFU content bridges — case studies, ROI calculators, comparison pages — that convert that traffic into pipeline
questions.d: Cut blog production and invest all resources into paid search

questions.question: Which search intent type describes a user searching "how to remove a stripped screw"?
questions.a: Informational
questions.b: Commercial investigation
questions.c: Transactional
questions.d: Navigational

questions.question: A page targeting "project management software" ranks well but has a very high bounce rate. The keyword has commercial investigation intent. What is the most likely cause?
questions.a: The page lacks enough internal links
questions.b: The page load speed is too slow
questions.c: The page title does not include the exact keyword phrase
questions.d: The page is a product landing page with pricing, but users at this stage want comparison content, not a sales pitch

questions.question: Google updates its algorithm and a pillar page that ranked #1 for a high-volume informational keyword drops to page 3. The SERP is now dominated by step-by-step listicles. The current page is a long-form essay. What is the correct diagnosis and fix?
questions.a: Split the page into multiple shorter pages to reduce word count
questions.b: The dominant content format has shifted — rewrite the page to match the listicle format Google now considers the best answer for this intent
questions.c: Build more backlinks to restore authority
questions.d: Google's quality raters flagged it for E-E-A-T issues — add author bios and citations

questions.question: A startup has a product useful to freelancers, agencies, and enterprise teams. Why choose a beachhead market first?
questions.a: To concentrate learning, positioning, distribution, and proof in the segment where adoption is most winnable
questions.b: To make the total addressable market look smaller and more credible
questions.c: To avoid building product features for future segments
questions.d: To reduce brand awareness spend by ignoring most buyers forever

questions.question: Two segments are attractive: Segment A has larger TAM but slow sales cycles; Segment B is smaller but has urgent pain, clear access channels, and high willingness to switch. Which is the stronger beachhead?
questions.a: Segment A, because the largest TAM should always drive GTM priority
questions.b: Segment B, because urgency, access, and switching likelihood make early traction and proof more achievable
questions.c: Split resources equally to avoid choosing wrong too early
questions.d: Target both with the same message and let performance data decide

questions.question: A company wins in its initial beachhead but struggles to expand. New segments do not respond to the original proof or use case. What should the GTM team do?
questions.a: Increase awareness spend because the new segments simply do not know the brand yet
questions.b: Keep the original positioning consistent because changing it would dilute the brand
questions.c: Define the expansion bridge: which adjacent segment shares the same pain, proof, buying trigger, or distribution path, then adapt positioning before scaling
questions.d: Move directly to the largest segment now that the brand has early traction

questions.question: A campaign drives $100K revenue, but product margin is low and fulfilment costs are high. What metric prevents the team from overclaiming success?
questions.a: Click-through rate, because it shows whether demand was created efficiently
questions.b: Gross traffic volume, because more visitors create future remarketing pools
questions.c: Total revenue, because marketing is responsible for top-line growth
questions.d: Contribution margin after variable costs, not revenue alone

questions.question: A promotion lifts revenue by 30% but contribution margin drops by 18%. What should marketing conclude?
questions.a: The promotion worked because revenue growth is the primary marketing goal
questions.b: The discount should be increased further to recover margin through higher volume
questions.c: The promotion may be buying unprofitable demand; evaluate incremental profit, cannibalisation, and whether customers would have bought anyway
questions.d: The campaign should be judged only on new customer count, not margin

questions.question: A fashion brand wants to scale paid media. ROAS is 3.5x, gross margin is 45%, return rate is 28%, and fulfilment costs are rising. What is the right executive question?
questions.a: Does the campaign generate positive contribution profit after returns, discounts, fulfilment, and media costs at the next marginal spend level?
questions.b: Can the team maintain 3.5x platform ROAS while increasing spend?
questions.c: Can creative improvements reduce CPM enough to keep acquisition scalable?
questions.d: Can the brand negotiate lower agency fees before increasing budget?

questions.question: In the StoryBrand framework, who is the "hero" of the story?
questions.a: The product or solution being sold
questions.b: The customer
questions.c: The CEO or company spokesperson
questions.d: The brand and its founding story

questions.question: A company's homepage says "We are the industry-leading platform trusted by 5,000 companies." According to StoryBrand, what is wrong with this message?
questions.a: The homepage lacks a clear call to action above the fold
questions.b: "Industry-leading" is too vague and needs a specific metric
questions.c: The social proof number is not large enough to be credible
questions.d: The brand is positioning itself as the hero instead of the customer — the message is about the company, not the customer's problem and transformation

questions.question: Using StoryBrand's 7-part framework, a cybersecurity firm wants to rewrite its homepage. Their current version lists 12 product features. What structure best applies the framework?
questions.a: Brand story → Mission statement → Team credentials → Product features → Case studies
questions.b: Awareness hook → Feature list → Competitive comparison → Risk reversal → CTA
questions.c: Hero (customer) faces a problem → Guide (brand) empathises and shows authority → Plan → Call to action → Success vision vs failure stakes
questions.d: Problem → Solution → Features → Pricing → Testimonials → FAQ → Contact

questions.question: In a freemium model, what is the primary mechanism that converts free users into paying customers?
questions.a: Sales reps who outreach to high-usage free accounts
questions.b: Ads shown to free users within the product
questions.c: Users experience value from the product and hit a limit or feature gate that incentivises upgrading
questions.d: Email drip campaigns sent after a 7-day trial expires

questions.question: A project management tool has a freemium tier with 3% free-to-paid conversion. Analysis shows most free users never invite a team member. What is the most strategic intervention?
questions.a: Shorten the freemium feature set to force upgrades sooner
questions.b: Launch a referral programme rewarding free users with premium months for each friend referred
questions.c: Add a prominent upgrade banner on the free plan dashboard
questions.d: Make team collaboration the core free experience — drive the "invite a teammate" moment early, because collaborative usage increases perceived value and conversion

questions.question: A B2B freemium SaaS has 200K free users converting at 1.2%. CAC from paid acquisition is $480. Freemium users cost $18/month to serve. ARPU is $120/month. Which statement is most analytically correct about evaluating freemium ROI vs. paid acquisition?
questions.a: The comparison also requires churn rate data — conversion rate alone is insufficient to evaluate freemium ROI versus paid acquisition
questions.b: Freemium beats paid acquisition at any conversion rate above 0% because acquisition cost is zero
questions.c: 4% conversion is the break-even because $18/month × 55-month payback exceeds CAC
questions.d: 2% conversion makes freemium cheaper because revenue offsets server costs

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a customer health score in B2B SaaS?
questions.a: To measure the performance of the customer success team
questions.b: To calculate the net promoter score across the customer base
questions.c: To rank prospects by likelihood to purchase for sales prioritisation
questions.d: To predict which existing customers are at risk of churning or likely to expand

questions.question: A customer health model uses only login frequency as its signal and churn prediction accuracy is poor. What signal categories would most improve the model?
questions.a: Add social media mentions and review site ratings
questions.b: Add product depth signals (features used, integrations enabled), support ticket sentiment, and engagement with success content alongside usage frequency
questions.c: Add the customer's company revenue and employee count from firmographic data
questions.d: Add sales cycle length and original deal size as predictors

questions.question: A CS team's health model flags 12% of accounts as "red" each quarter. Only 30% of those red accounts actually churn, and 40% of accounts that churn were never flagged. What two model problems does this describe?
questions.a: Low precision (too many false positives) and low recall (too many false negatives) — retrain with better-labelled historical churn data and tune the classification threshold
questions.b: High precision and high recall — the model is working and the CS team needs more headcount
questions.c: The scoring is non-linear — switch from a weighted score to a machine learning classifier
questions.d: Data leakage — remove future-dated variables and retrain from scratch

questions.question: What does PIE stand for in the CRO prioritisation framework?
questions.a: Performance, Impact, Effort
questions.b: Priority, Intent, Engagement
questions.c: Potential, Importance, Ease
questions.d: Page Interaction Events

questions.question: A CRO team has 10 test ideas. The checkout page has the highest traffic and worst conversion rate in the funnel. Which PIE criteria combination best justifies prioritising the checkout test first?
questions.a: The checkout page should always be tested first regardless of PIE scores
questions.b: High Potential (large conversion gap) + High Importance (checkout drives all revenue) + High Ease (simple copy change) — scores highest overall
questions.c: Medium Potential + Low Importance + High Ease — easy tests should go first to build momentum
questions.d: PIE scores are irrelevant for checkout pages; use session recordings to decide instead

questions.question: A growth team uses PIE scoring but top-ranked tests consistently underperform predictions. Post-analysis shows Potential scores were based on gut feel. What systemic change best improves PIE scoring accuracy?
questions.a: Base Potential scores on quantitative data — conversion gap analysis from funnel reports, heatmaps, and session recordings — rather than subjective estimates
questions.b: Switch from PIE to ICE scoring, which uses a Confidence metric instead of Importance
questions.c: Lower the minimum Ease threshold so only quick-win tests are run
questions.d: Hire an external CRO consultant to calibrate scores against industry benchmarks

questions.question: What psychological principle does anchor pricing exploit?
questions.a: Loss aversion — people fear losing money more than they value equivalent gains
questions.b: The first price seen creates a reference point that makes subsequent prices feel relatively cheaper or more expensive
questions.c: Social proof — people choose options others have already chosen
questions.d: The decoy effect — adding a third option shifts preference between two existing choices

questions.question: A SaaS company displays Starter $29 / Pro $79 / Enterprise $299. Most users choose Pro. If the Enterprise tier is removed, what outcome is most likely according to anchoring research?
questions.a: Users split evenly between Starter and Pro without the high anchor
questions.b: Users upgrade more since there is one fewer option to evaluate
questions.c: Removing Enterprise has no effect since most users already chose Pro
questions.d: Pro becomes the most expensive option — perceived value drops and Pro conversion declines

questions.question: A consulting firm wants to shift clients toward a $25K engagement. The current menu shows $5K, $15K, and $25K options but win rates on $25K are low. Which restructuring best applies anchoring theory?
questions.a: Add a $60K "premium partnership" tier above $25K — the high anchor makes $25K feel like the reasonable middle choice
questions.b: Remove the $5K option entirely to eliminate the low-value anchor
questions.c: Switch to custom quotes so clients have no price anchor at all
questions.d: Rename the $25K tier "Most Popular" to add social proof alongside the anchor

questions.question: Pipeline acceleration tactics are primarily designed to do what?
questions.a: Reduce CAC by automating outbound outreach
questions.b: Increase the number of leads entering the top of the funnel
questions.c: Improve inbound lead quality through better targeting
questions.d: Shorten the time deals spend in specific stages and move them to close faster

questions.question: CRM data shows 35% of deals stall in "technical evaluation" for more than 45 days. Which pipeline acceleration tactic most directly addresses this stage?
questions.a: Launch a retargeting campaign to re-engage the buying committee with case study ads
questions.b: Offer a 20% discount if the prospect signs within 30 days
questions.c: Introduce a structured technical win plan — dedicated solution engineer, sandbox access, and a defined evaluation checklist with a mutual success deadline
questions.d: Assign an SDR to send follow-up emails every 3 days

questions.question: RevOps analysis shows average sales cycle is 87 days, with 60% of time in "proposal review" (avg 22 days) and "legal review" (avg 30 days). What combined intervention most effectively compresses cycle time?
questions.a: Hire more AEs to handle more deals in parallel
questions.b: Use a standard MSA with pre-negotiated redlines to reduce legal back-and-forth; introduce mutual action plans with champion-owned proposal review milestones and an executive sponsor touchpoint
questions.c: Move to a land-and-expand model that closes a smaller initial deal faster
questions.d: Automate follow-up so no deal goes 48 hours without contact during these stages

questions.question: What is an Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) used for?
questions.a: Defining the persona of the end user who uses the product daily
questions.b: Creating audience targeting parameters for paid media campaigns
questions.c: Segmenting the existing customer base by NPS score
questions.d: Identifying the type of company most likely to get maximum value from the product, stay long-term, and expand

questions.question: A sales team closes deals across many verticals but churn is high and expansion revenue is low. How should RevOps use CRM data to refine the ICP?
questions.a: Use the largest deals by ACV as the ICP, since high ACV correlates with long-term fit
questions.b: Analyse closed-won deals by LTV, time-to-value, expansion rate, and NPS — find the firmographic and technographic patterns in the top-performing cohort and define ICP around those signals
questions.c: Define ICP based on the industry with the most inbound leads
questions.d: Survey the sales team on which deals were easiest to close

questions.question: A startup's ICP is "Series B SaaS, 50-200 employees, using Salesforce." Pipeline velocity is fast but win rates against one competitor are near zero. What ICP refinement approach gives the most actionable signal?
questions.a: Remove Salesforce as an ICP criterion since it doesn't predict win rate
questions.b: Broaden the ICP to Series A to increase the addressable pool
questions.c: Layer competitive displacement data into the ICP — identify firmographic or technographic signals that correlate with wins vs losses against that competitor specifically
questions.d: Focus exclusively on accounts the competitor already serves

questions.question: Which technical record helps receiving servers verify that a domain is authorised to send email on its behalf?
questions.a: A record
questions.b: SPF record
questions.c: CNAME record
questions.d: MX record

questions.question: An email programme sees open rates drop from 28% to 11% over three months with no list or content changes. What deliverability issue is most likely, and what is the first diagnostic step?
questions.a: iOS Mail Privacy Protection is skewing open rates — switch to click rate as the primary metric
questions.b: The ESP has changed its sending infrastructure — contact support to restore the original IP pool
questions.c: Sender reputation has degraded — check the domain's reputation score, review bounce and complaint rates, and run a seed list test to check inbox placement
questions.d: Subject line fatigue — A/B test new subject lines before diagnosing technical issues

questions.question: A marketing team acquires 50K contacts through a co-registration partner and wants to email them immediately. The list has never been mailed. What is the most technically correct approach to protect deliverability?
questions.a: Send the full list in one batch at 9am to maximise launch day reach
questions.b: Import the list into a new subdomain to isolate any deliverability issues from the main domain
questions.c: Co-registration lists are CAN-SPAM compliant by nature — no special treatment is needed
questions.d: Validate and clean the list first; warm the sending IP by gradually ramping volume — start with 500/day, doubling every 2-3 days — while monitoring spam complaint rates and adjusting if complaints exceed 0.1%

questions.question: What is "dark social" in the context of marketing attribution?
questions.a: Social posts published outside business hours to avoid algorithm throttling
questions.b: Negative social media conversations about a brand that are difficult to monitor
questions.c: Sharing of content via private channels (DMs, Slack, email, WhatsApp) that appears as direct traffic — the source is unattributable
questions.d: Paid social campaigns with no public-facing creative, targeted only to known customer lists

questions.question: A B2B company notices that 45% of traffic to its pricing page is classified as "direct" in Google Analytics, but brand awareness is growing strongly. What is the most plausible explanation?
questions.a: Users are bookmarking the pricing page after seeing ads and returning later
questions.b: A large portion of that "direct" traffic is dark social — prospects share pricing links in Slack and private communities where UTM parameters are stripped
questions.c: The UTM tracking on paid campaigns is broken and needs to be rebuilt
questions.d: Direct traffic always overstates volume — this is a normal Google Analytics sampling artefact

questions.question: A CMO wants to prove that dark social is driving pipeline. What combination of methods best builds an evidence-based case?
questions.a: Survey prospects at demo request ("how did you hear about us?"), analyse self-reported attribution vs UTM data gaps, and run branded keyword search trend analysis against content distribution events to triangulate dark social impact
questions.b: Switch all attribution to last-touch so unattributed traffic is excluded from the model
questions.c: Use the Facebook conversion API to recover missing attribution from iOS privacy changes
questions.d: Install a heatmapping tool on the pricing page to understand how prospects interact once they arrive

questions.question: Expansion MRR is generated when existing customers do what?
questions.a: Upgrade their plan, add seats, or purchase additional products
questions.b: Renew their contract at the same price
questions.c: Refer new customers who then sign a contract
questions.d: Move from monthly to annual billing

questions.question: A SaaS company has negative net revenue churn. What does this indicate?
questions.a: The churn rate calculation has an error because revenue churn cannot be negative
questions.b: The company is losing more customers than it is gaining
questions.c: Expansion revenue from existing customers more than offsets revenue lost from churned customers — the customer base grows in value even without new logo acquisition
questions.d: Customer success is discounting renewals below original contract value

questions.question: A usage-based SaaS has $2M ARR, 8% gross churn, and 18% expansion rate. A product-led motion is proposed where hitting a usage milestone triggers an in-app upgrade prompt. What metric best evaluates whether the motion is working after 90 days?
questions.a: DAU/MAU ratio, because engagement predicts future expansion
questions.b: Expansion MRR attributed to the in-app prompt, compared against the baseline expansion rate in a holdout cohort that does not see the prompt
questions.c: Total ARR growth, since expansion and churn effects are both captured in that single metric
questions.d: Gross churn rate — if the motion works, churn should decrease as customers get more value

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of social proof in a marketing context?
questions.a: A personalised product recommendation based on browsing history
questions.b: A money-back guarantee to reduce purchase risk
questions.c: A homepage displaying customer logos, review counts, and testimonials
questions.d: A countdown timer showing a limited-time offer

questions.question: An e-commerce brand adds star ratings to product pages and sees a 9% lift in add-to-cart rate. However, products with fewer than 5 reviews see no lift. What explains this, and what is the fix?
questions.a: The star rating widget is not rendering correctly on mobile for low-review products — fix the CSS
questions.b: Below a social proof threshold, sparse reviews reduce credibility rather than building it — hide review counts below 5 and instead display bestseller badges or "X people bought this" signals until reviews accumulate
questions.c: Products with few reviews have lower prices — bundle them with higher-rated products
questions.d: Low-review products have worse descriptions — improve copy to compensate for lack of reviews

questions.question: A B2B SaaS product page has a 1.4% demo request rate. Social proof includes a generic "Trusted by thousands" badge and three short testimonials. What evidence-based restructuring would most improve conversion?
questions.a: Add a video testimonial autoplay reel above the fold to maximise time-on-page
questions.b: Remove all social proof to reduce page clutter and focus on the CTA
questions.c: Increase the size of the "Trusted by thousands" badge and add an animated counter
questions.d: Replace generic claims with specific, named customer proof — logo wall of ICP logos, quantified outcome quotes ("cut reporting time by 60%"), and a G2 review widget — placing the strongest proof adjacent to the CTA

questions.question: Lead scoring combines two types of data. Which pair correctly describes them?
questions.a: Traffic source and time on site
questions.b: Demographic / firmographic fit (explicit) and behavioural engagement (implicit)
questions.c: Campaign spend and cost per lead
questions.d: Lead volume and close rate by channel

questions.question: MQLs passed from marketing convert to pipeline at only 8%, far below the 25% target. What is the most likely scoring model problem?
questions.a: Marketing needs to send more nurture emails before passing leads so contacts are more warmed up
questions.b: Sales needs better discovery training to convert the leads they are receiving
questions.c: The MQL threshold is too high — lower it so more leads are passed to sales
questions.d: The model is over-weighting engagement signals like email opens, which inflate scores for unqualified contacts — it needs to weight fit criteria (title, company size, industry) more heavily

questions.question: A marketing ops team wants to build a predictive lead score using 10,000 closed-won and closed-lost deals from the past two years. What is the single most important data quality check before building the model?
questions.a: Verify all leads have a complete set of 20+ firmographic fields before including them
questions.b: Remove all deals under $5K ACV since they are not representative of the target market
questions.c: Ensure the win/loss label is reliable — check for deals marked lost that were actually cancelled, stale deals never properly dispositioned, and recency bias if win rates changed significantly in the past 6 months
questions.d: Confirm the dataset is balanced — downsample won deals to match the number of lost deals before training

questions.question: The "content distribution" step in a content marketing workflow refers to what?
questions.a: Actively getting published content in front of the right audience through owned, earned, and paid channels
questions.b: Repurposing long-form content into shorter formats
questions.c: Deciding which team member writes each piece of content
questions.d: Tracking how content ranks in search results after publication

questions.question: A B2B content team publishes two posts per week but organic traffic has plateaued. Distribution is limited to the blog and one LinkedIn post. What is the highest-leverage distribution expansion?
questions.a: Increase production to four posts per week to compound SEO gains faster
questions.b: Audit existing content for quick SEO wins, then build a multi-channel distribution workflow: LinkedIn native posts, newsletter syndication, community sharing, and employee amplification — more distribution from fewer new pieces
questions.c: Repurpose every post into a Twitter/X thread to reach a new audience
questions.d: Launch a paid content syndication campaign to drive traffic to existing posts

questions.question: A content programme has 200+ published assets. 80% of traffic goes to 12% of posts. The team produces 8 new posts per month. What resource allocation maximises content ROI?
questions.a: Stop all new production until all existing content is audited and refreshed
questions.b: Delete all posts in the bottom 88% of traffic to concentrate site authority
questions.c: Continue at the same production rate — new posts compound into traffic over 12-18 months
questions.d: Shift 40-50% of production budget to updating and redistributing high-performing content, build topical clusters around the top 12% to capture related keyword demand, and use the remaining budget on new posts targeting identified gaps

questions.question: Net Revenue Retention (NRR) above 100% means what for a SaaS business?
questions.a: The company has more new customers than churned customers this period
questions.b: The company's gross margin is above 100%, indicating negative COGS
questions.c: All customers renewed their contracts with no downgrades
questions.d: Revenue from existing customers is growing — expansion revenue exceeds churn and contraction combined

questions.question: A company has 120% NRR and 15% logo churn. What does this combination tell you, and what risk does it reveal?
questions.a: Revenue is growing from existing accounts but the company is losing a significant number of customers — likely smaller accounts churn while large accounts expand, creating concentration risk and masking acquisition problems
questions.b: The 15% logo churn is within normal SaaS range and the 120% NRR indicates strong product-market fit across all segments
questions.c: The NRR calculation is incorrect — NRR cannot exceed 100% if logo churn is above 5%
questions.d: The business is healthy with no risks — high NRR more than compensates for any churn

questions.question: A CFO wants to improve NRR from 105% to 120% within 12 months without increasing headcount. Which lever combination has the highest expected impact on NRR specifically?
questions.a: Launch a new product tier priced 40% above current plans and migrate all customers to it
questions.b: Build a usage-based expansion trigger (automated upsell prompt at 80% of plan limit), launch a QBR programme for accounts over $10K ARR focused on expansion, and introduce a formalised churn save playbook with win-back offers for at-risk accounts
questions.c: Focus all CS resources on onboarding new customers faster so they expand earlier
questions.d: Reduce prices by 20% to improve retention rates, which will lift NRR

questions.question: What fundamentally distinguishes ABM from broad demand generation?
questions.a: ABM is only for enterprise companies; demand gen is for SMB and mid-market
questions.b: ABM measures success by MQL volume; demand gen measures by pipeline value
questions.c: ABM uses only outbound channels while demand gen uses only inbound
questions.d: ABM targets specific high-value accounts with personalised programmes rather than casting a wide net to generate leads in bulk

questions.question: An ABM programme targets 200 enterprise accounts. After 6 months, pipeline from target accounts is low despite high impression share. Sales says engagement is low. What is the most likely problem?
questions.a: The ABM platform is not syncing correctly with the CRM — fix the integration before evaluating results
questions.b: ABM requires 12+ months to show pipeline — report back in another 6 months
questions.c: The personalisation is too shallow — ads and outreach use only company name substitution without addressing the specific business problem or buying committee stage
questions.d: The target account list is too small — expand to 1,000 accounts

questions.question: A revenue team debates "1:1 ABM" (highly customised per account) vs "1:many ABM" (personalised by segment). They have 2 enterprise AEs and 1 marketing person for ABM. Which strategy is correct and how should measurement differ from demand gen?
questions.a: 1:1 ABM is correct and should be measured by total impressions across the target account list
questions.b: 1:1 ABM is correct for enterprise but should be measured by pipeline created per target account, deal velocity in named accounts, and multi-threaded contact coverage — not by MQL volume or CPL metrics
questions.c: Neither — with 1 marketing person ABM is not viable; all resources should go to inbound SEO
questions.d: 1:many ABM is correct given resource constraints — measure by MQL volume just like demand gen

questions.question: A subscription brand has CAC of $180 and monthly gross profit per customer of $30. What does payback period help the team understand?
questions.a: How many months customers stay before they churn
questions.b: How quickly ad platforms optimise after launch
questions.c: How long it takes to recover acquisition cost from customer gross profit
questions.d: How much revenue the customer generates before discounts

questions.question: Channel A has lower CAC but customers churn after 2 months. Channel B has higher CAC but customers stay 14 months and expand. Which budget logic is correct?
questions.a: Prioritise Channel A because lower CAC means more efficient growth
questions.b: Split budget evenly because the channels balance short- and long-term outcomes
questions.c: Prioritise Channel B only if its first-purchase ROAS is higher
questions.d: Allocate based on LTV-to-CAC and payback, not CAC alone, because acquisition cost without customer quality is incomplete

questions.question: A SaaS company can grow ARR faster by accepting 18-month CAC payback, but cash reserves cover only 12 months of current burn. What should leadership consider?
questions.a: Take the growth because ARR scale improves valuation even if payback is long
questions.b: Growth rate must be constrained by cash payback and retention quality; efficient growth is not just high ARR if cash conversion is too slow
questions.c: Cut acquisition until CAC payback is under 3 months
questions.d: Shift all spend to brand because payback is harder to attribute there

questions.question: What does a retention cohort chart measure?
questions.a: Revenue generated by each marketing channel over time
questions.b: The lifetime value of customers grouped by acquisition channel
questions.c: The percentage of users from a specific starting period who are still active at each subsequent time interval
questions.d: How long it takes new users to complete their first purchase

questions.question: A cohort chart shows Day 1 retention of 40% across all cohorts, but Day 30 retention improving from 8% to 18% over 6 months of product changes. What does this pattern indicate?
questions.a: Early activation (D1) remains a problem but long-term habit formation is improving — the product changes are working for users who get past the initial drop, but early onboarding still needs fixing
questions.b: The data is inconsistent — D30 retention cannot improve if D1 retention stays flat
questions.c: The product has reached product-market fit, since monthly retention is approaching 20%
questions.d: Acquisition quality has improved — newer cohorts are better qualified users

questions.question: Two acquisition channels show identical Day 30 retention (22%). However, Channel A customers have 3x higher expansion revenue at Month 6. What is the strategic implication for budget allocation?
questions.a: Split budget equally since retention parity proves both channels deliver equivalent customer quality
questions.b: Retention at 30 days is the definitive quality metric — expansion data beyond 30 days is too speculative for budget decisions
questions.c: Investigate whether Channel A customers are gaming the expansion mechanism before reallocating budget
questions.d: Channel A delivers customers with higher growth potential — retention alone is an incomplete quality signal, and budget should shift toward Channel A with LTV-to-CAC as the primary allocation metric rather than retention rate

questions.question: In Osterwalder's Value Proposition Canvas, what two sides does it map?
questions.a: Marketing channels and customer acquisition costs
questions.b: Customer Profile (jobs, pains, gains) and Value Map (products, pain relievers, gain creators)
questions.c: Product features and pricing tiers
questions.d: Brand positioning and competitive differentiation

questions.question: A B2B product team writes: "Our platform saves time and improves efficiency." Using the Value Proposition Canvas, what is wrong with this statement?
questions.a: It is correct — efficiency and time savings are universally valued and need no further specificity
questions.b: It should include pricing to be a complete value proposition
questions.c: It is too long — value propositions should be one word or phrase
questions.d: It addresses gain creators but does not map to a specific customer job or pain — "saves time" is generic and not grounded in a concrete, observable customer struggle

questions.question: Two competitors offer the same core feature set at the same price. How should a product marketing team use the Value Proposition Canvas to find a defensible differentiation angle?
questions.a: Compete on price — when features and positioning are equivalent, cost is the only differentiator
questions.b: Rewrite messaging to emphasise the company's founding story and values as the differentiator
questions.c: Run customer interviews to deeply map the highest-intensity unsolved pains and unmet gains — find a pain reliever or gain creator the market underserves, and build positioning and product prioritisation around that gap
questions.d: Add more features faster than the competitor to create differentiation through product breadth

questions.question: Research on video ad performance consistently shows the most critical moment for viewer retention is which part?
questions.a: The middle section where the main message is delivered
questions.b: The end card where the CTA is displayed
questions.c: The first 3 seconds — where the hook must stop the scroll
questions.d: The audio track — sound quality predicts completion rate

questions.question: A paid social video ad achieves 65% video completion rate but generates almost no clicks or conversions. What is the most likely creative problem?
questions.a: The targeting is wrong — high completion rate indicates the wrong audience is watching
questions.b: The video is too short — under 30 seconds cannot build enough trust for a conversion
questions.c: The landing page is the problem, not the creative — strong completion rates prove the ad is working
questions.d: The CTA is buried or appears only at the end — viewers are engaged but the conversion action is not clearly presented at the peak engagement moment

questions.question: A DTC brand runs 8 video ad variations and finds one "ugly," unpolished UGC-style video significantly outperforms all polished brand videos on ROAS. How should the creative team respond?
questions.a: Continue running both and report back after the UGC ad fatigues — the win is likely due to novelty
questions.b: The UGC format builds authenticity and trust that polished ads lack here — introduce a systematic UGC production and testing track alongside brand video, using performance data (not aesthetic preference) to guide scaling decisions
questions.c: Replace all brand video production with UGC immediately since the data proves UGC always outperforms
questions.d: The result is an anomaly — polished brand video is required to maintain brand safety and the outlier should be paused

results.title: T-Shaped Strategic Operator
results.description: Broad coverage across the map plus deep spikes and mature business judgement. You diagnose, prioritise and manage trade-offs across the full system.
results.learningPath: Deepen your competitive strategy and GTM leadership muscles. Focus on P&L fluency, cross-functional influence, and org design for marketing functions.

results.title: Full-Stack Marketer
results.description: You confidently connect strategy, channels, analytics, lifecycle and revenue. Strong diagnostic instinct across the system with some gaps in advanced judgement.
results.learningPath: Close your executive-level gaps: prioritisation frameworks, budget allocation under uncertainty, and board-level narrative. Strengthen your weakest domain.

results.title: Functional Generalist
results.description: Good breadth, but depth and judgement are uneven. You know a lot but tend to solve with templates rather than diagnosis.
results.learningPath: Pick your two weakest domains and go deep. Practise diagnostic thinking: when you see a metric problem, ask why at least 3 levels before jumping to a solution.

results.title: Developing Marketer
results.description: You can execute in specific zones but need stronger diagnostic thinking. Building the connective tissue between domains is the key growth lever.
results.learningPath: Prioritise: Analytics & Experimentation + one strategic domain. Learn to read dashboards diagnostically, not just descriptively. Take on a growth experiment end-to-end.

results.title: Tactical Executor
results.description: You recognise individual terms and platforms. The next step is building the system view that connects tools to business outcomes.
results.learningPath: Start with Strategy & Market Thinking fundamentals: JTBD, ICP, value proposition. Then layer in one channel deeply. Understand how each tool connects to a revenue outcome before moving to the next.
